_meta.purpose: CPA task-based simulations (TBS) in exam style. Each row is scored separately, as in the real exam. Original content.

tasks.title: Operating cash flow worksheet
tasks.scenario: Darwin Co. reports net income of $250,000. During the year: depreciation $40,000; accounts receivable increased $30,000; inventory decreased $10,000; accounts payable decreased $15,000; gain on sale of equipment $8,000. Enter each adjustment to net income (use a minus sign for deductions) and the resulting cash from operating activities (indirect method).
tasks.explain: Add back non-cash expenses. Subtract gains (the cash proceeds go to investing). Subtract increases in current assets and add decreases. Add increases in current liabilities and subtract decreases. 250,000 + 40,000 − 30,000 + 10,000 − 15,000 − 8,000 = 247,000.

tasks.title: Bond amortisation schedule
tasks.scenario: On 1 Jan Year 1, Kepler Inc. issued bonds with face value $500,000 and a 6% annual coupon paid each 31 Dec, for $480,000 (market rate 7%). Using the effective interest method, complete the schedule. Round to whole dollars.
tasks.explain: Expense = opening carrying amount × 7%. Cash = 500,000 × 6%. The difference is amortisation, which increases the carrying amount towards face. Year 2: 483,600 × 7% = 33,852, so the carrying amount becomes 483,600 + 3,852 = 487,452.

tasks.title: Classify cash flows (US GAAP)
tasks.scenario: For each item, select the section of the statement of cash flows where it is reported under US GAAP.

rows.label: Acquisition of land by issuing common stock
Interest received on a loan to a supplier

tasks.explain: US GAAP: interest paid and received and dividends received are operating; dividends paid are financing; buying long-term assets is investing; issuing debt or equity is financing; non-cash exchanges are disclosed separately.

tasks.title: Match procedures to assertions
tasks.scenario: For each audit procedure, select the PRIMARY assertion it tests.

rows.label: Confirm accounts receivable balances with customers
Trace shipping documents to the sales journal
Review cash collected from customers after year-end
Inspect the title deed for land
Examine sales invoices from the last 5 days of the year and the first 5 days of the next year
Search for unrecorded liabilities by examining payments made after year-end

tasks.explain: Vouching from records to evidence tests existence. Tracing from source documents to records, and searching for unrecorded items, tests completeness. Subsequent receipts support collectability (valuation). Title documents prove rights. Transactions around year-end test cut-off.

tasks.title: Select the auditor's report
tasks.scenario: For each independent situation, select the appropriate type of auditor's report.

rows.label: Inventory is overstated materially, but the effect is confined to inventory and COGS
The company failed to consolidate a major subsidiary; misstatements affect most line items
Records were destroyed in a fire and the auditor cannot obtain evidence for most balances
Substantial doubt about going concern, adequately disclosed
Auditor could not observe the inventory count; other procedures failed; inventory is material but not pervasive

tasks.explain: Use the 2×2 grid: misstatement (material → qualified, pervasive → adverse) and inability to obtain evidence (material → qualified, pervasive → disclaimer). Going concern with adequate disclosure keeps an unmodified opinion, with a separate section.

tasks.title: Partner's outside basis
tasks.scenario: Mira contributed $80,000 cash for a 25% partnership interest on 1 Jan. For the year, her distributive share was: ordinary business income $30,000 and tax-exempt interest $2,000. She received cash distributions of $25,000. Her share of partnership liabilities increased by $10,000. Complete her basis computation.

rows.label: Add: increase in share of liabilities

tasks.explain: Outside basis increases with contributions, ALL income (including tax-exempt) and increases in liability share. It decreases with distributions, losses and non-deductible expenses. 80,000 + 30,000 + 2,000 + 10,000 − 25,000 = 97,000.

tasks.title: Direct materials variances
tasks.scenario: Standard: 2 kg per unit at $5.00/kg. 1,000 units were produced. 2,200 kg were purchased and used at $4.80/kg. Enter each variance as a positive number and select favourable (F) or unfavourable (U).
